create.name: Dr. Jean Shinoda Bolen
create.bio:
Dr. Jean Shinoda Bolen is an American psychiatrist and Jungian analyst best known for her writing on the gods and goddesses of Greek myth as living patterns in the psyche. Born into a Japanese American family that was forced to leave California during the Second World War, she trained in medicine and psychiatry, qualified as an analyst at San Francisco's Jung Institute in the 1970s, and taught psychiatry at the University of California, San Francisco. Her books, published in many languages, include Goddesses in Everywoman, Gods in Everyman, The Tao of Psychology, Crossing to Avalon and Goddesses in Older Women, and more recently a memoir of her life and mystical experiences.

Her teaching joins myth, synchronicity and the inner life with care for the world. She invites people to recognise which archetypes are shaping them, to ask what their soul came here to do, and to follow a path with heart through every stage of life, especially later life. She inspired the Millionth Circle movement of women's sacred circles, has represented women's organisations at the United Nations, and has spoken at the Parliament of the World's Religions. Her recorded talks and short courses are available through Jung Platform, and she has also taught online courses with The Shift Network. She lives and works in Marin County, California.

videos.title: Becoming Who You Are Meant to Be with Jean Shinoda Bolen, MD

courses.title: Path of the Soul
courses.description: Three remastered recorded classes, about three hours in all, in which she mixes personal stories with Greek myth. They ask what you came here to do and how to reclaim the parts of yourself set aside on the way.

courses.title: Making Meaning of the Numinous
courses.description: A recorded ninety-minute talk on moments of awe, grace and synchronicity, how to recognise them and how to let them shape the course of a life.

courses.title: Catching Fire: Imagination, Creativity, Activism
courses.description: A recorded talk of about an hour and a half on imagination, creativity and compassionate action as part of becoming who you are, in the Jungian sense of individuation.
